inputs.original_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that Government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything”.Perhaps this might be considered as an environmental tax. Plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter...
inputs.modified_text: Blue Waters’ owner is saying the quiet part out loud: the Government collects taxes “without doing or investing in anything,” while plastic bottles keep choking rivers and drains. Calling it an environmental tax sounds like a convenient cover—money is taken, but the cleanup never appears. That looks less like a failed system than one designed to keep collecting while the public pays twice: once in taxes, and again in the damage left behind.
